description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of the SepLLM model and a baseline StrmLLM model, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with linear spacing and major tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Five distinct lines are plotted: StrmLLM (n=64) in blue with a solid line starts at approximately 3.35 and steadily decreases to around 2.62; SepLLM (n=64) in orange with a solid line begins near 3.3 and declines to about 2.55; SepLLM (n=64, H) in green with a solid line starts at ~3.3 and ends near 2.53; SepLLM (n=64, H/T) in red with a solid line begins at ~3.3 and converges to ~2.52; and SepLLM (n=128) in dark blue with a solid line starts at ~3.3 and ends near 2.51. All models exhibit a rapid initial drop in loss within the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a slower, steady decline toward convergence. The shaded region behind the legend appears to be a placeholder or artifact and does not correspond to any plotted data.
